source.title: I trained GPT-2 with full-batch gradient descent so you don't have to

record.file_problem: Full post and comments are present. The author flags methodological confounders and an untrusted 10× convergence run.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares full-batch and minibatch gradient training on a fixed language-model training set and reports training and validation losses, a different task and measure from the listed classification-error versions.
record.gate_note: The post reports its own GPT-2 training results and dynamics, which bear on the broad training claim. The cited Cohen et al. edge-of-stability work and other related work are not results of this study. Rows below cover the main fixed-set comparison, batch-size ladder, and full-batch pilots; the extensive fresh-data learning-rate sweeps and ablations do not directly test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study reports language-model training and validation losses, not V1's CIFAR classification error in convolutional networks. Its full-batch dynamics resemble edge-of-stability behavior, but it does not establish a stability threshold, sharpness tracking that threshold, or above-threshold recovery or divergence as specified in V5. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The author initially attributes the validation gap to batch-selection noise, then withdraws the claim that noise is essential and emphasizes inadequate retuning and other confounders. Even the broader inference that training-set fit alone is insufficient for generalization is presented as incompletely established.
record.recipe_differences: Full-batch GPT-2 language-model training on a fixed token set, using a speedrun-derived architecture and optimizer; it compares against minibatch training and measures language-model loss rather than classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size and repeated exposure to a fixed dataset changed the reported validation losses. The learning rate was tuned on fresh data rather than the fixed set; the author reports this as a confounder.

fits_no_version.finding: On the fixed 800M-token set, full batch reached training loss 3.094 versus 3.186 for small batch, but validation loss was 3.521 versus 3.248. Larger fixed-set minibatches also showed worse validation endpoints than fresh-data comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For this modified GPT-2 recipe, batch size and repeated token exposure affect the relationship between training fit and validation performance; the experiment does not isolate gradient noise from repetition or recipe tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: The 25M-token full-batch pilot memorized its dataset, reaching training loss 0.04 by step 224; smaller-set pilots showed overfitting in validation loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Full-batch training can memorize a small language-modeling dataset under this recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: The full-batch run had median consecutive-gradient cosine −0.945, approximately twofold directional overshooting, loss increases on about one third of steps, and growing top Hessian eigenvalues.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: This Muon-family full-batch run exhibits oscillatory training dynamics resembling edge-of-stability behavior, without establishing a quantitative stability boundary.

record.problems: One run per configuration for the main comparison; learning rate tuned on fresh data rather than the fixed set; many optimizer and schedule choices were tuned for a different setup; the full-batch fixed-set run makes 350 passes and therefore does not separate absence of gradient noise from repeated exposure; the 10× fresh-data convergence reference is explicitly distrusted because FP8 training and bf16 evaluation losses diverged. The author says the validation gap is larger than seed-to-seed noise but its exact size is not pinned down.
record.rows_left_out: Fresh-data runs and large-batch learning-rate sweeps do not test the claim versions' classification-error or above-stability-limit recovery outcomes. Additional ablation runs modify model components or schedule and report validation losses, but are comparisons of the training recipe rather than direct tests of the listed version-specific claims; not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: All specified CIFAR convolutional-network training classification-error outcomes, including random labels and capacity or recipe qualifications.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
Comparisons of initialization, training speed, and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, divergence at larger rates or from initially subthreshold runs, and sharpness tracking a quantified full-batch stability threshold.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparison with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The tabulated values are supported by the supplied text. All model subjects should be described as modified speedrun-derived GPT-2 configurations: the hash table, sampled softmax, and changing-objective schedules were removed. Generalization gaps cannot limit a claim solely about training fit. The absence of a stability-threshold test is untested scope, not a limits_scope verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Tests training-set fit under full-batch versus minibatch training on a language-modeling objective, not classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, or smaller model capacity.

Reports edge-of-stability dynamics and Hessian eigenvalues for a Muon-family optimizer, but does not compare learning rates above and below the initial linearized-model stability limit or report the recovery/divergence test described in the version.
